title: Metrics 101
objectives: Master the core metrics: Impressions, Reach, Frequency, CPM, CTR, CPC, CPL, and ROAS
Calculate ad efficiency using simple metric formulas
Understand the story each metric tells about your campaign

blocks.text: Metrics are the vital signs of your campaign! When you know what they mean, you can fix any problem.
Let's break down the essential numbers you will see on your Ads Manager dashboard every morning.

rows: Total times ad appeared on screen
Total unique people who saw it
Average times each person saw it
Average cost paid for one click
Cost to get one lead or inquiry

blocks.title: The Shop Window Analogy
blocks.text: CPM is the rent for your shop window. CTR is how many passers-by stop and walk inside. CVR is how many of those visitors actually buy. ROAS is your profit multiple!
A good CTR in India on mobile feeds is typically between 1.2% and 2.5%.
If Frequency climbs above 3.5 on a cold audience, fatigue is setting in. People are getting tired of your ad!

quiz.q: Your campaign spent ₹5,000 and generated ₹25,000 in online orders. What is your ROAS?
quiz.hint: Divide total revenue generated by total ad spend.
quiz.explain: ₹25,000 ÷ ₹5,000 = 5.0x ROAS. For every ₹1 spent, you made ₹5 back!

quiz.q: Your ad was shown 20,000 times to 10,000 unique people. What is the frequency?
quiz.explain: 20,000 ÷ 10,000 = 2.0. On average, each person saw the ad twice.

quiz.q: What metric tells you how compelling and scroll-stopping your ad creative is?
quiz.hint: Which metric measures the percentage of people who decided to click?
quiz.explain: CTR reflects creative appeal. High CTR means your visual and headline successfully hook the audience.

quiz.q: If an ad set spent ₹1,500 and delivered 10,000 impressions, what is the CPM?

recap: CPM = cost per 1,000 views. CTR = interest in the ad. CPL = cost per contact.
ROAS = Revenue ÷ Spend. Keep frequency below 3.5 on cold prospects.
